summary.text: Ancient Egypt was a cradle of civilization concentrated along the lower reaches of the Nile River in the eastern part of North Africa.
It emerged around 3150 BC, when Upper and Lower Egypt were united by Menes, and its history alternated stable kingdoms with periods of relative instability.
The predictable flooding of the Nile and controlled irrigation produced surplus crops that supported a denser population and substantial social and cultural development.

facts.label: Peak of power
facts.value: The New Kingdom, known as the Egyptian Empire

facts.label: Dynasty system
facts.value: Manetho grouped the kings into 30 dynasties

facts.label: Early capital
facts.value: Memphis, set up to control the fertile delta

items.prompt: The Nile flooded on a predictable schedule and farmers irrigated the valley. What did that give Egyptian society?

options.label: Plenty of trade goods from Nubia
Surplus crops supporting more people
A military that conquered the Levant
Walls that guarded the river

items.explain: Predictable flooding and irrigation produced surplus crops, which supported a denser population.

items.prompt: Egypt's power peaked in one of its stable kingdom periods, when its rule reached much of Nubia and part of the Levant. Which period?

options.label: The Old Kingdom
The Middle Kingdom
The New Kingdom
The Predynastic Period

items.explain: The pinnacle of power came in the New Kingdom, known as the Egyptian Empire.

items.prompt: Ancient Egyptian writers described a clean unification of the two kingdoms. What do modern scholars say about how it happened?

options.label: It came about more gradually than they claimed
It was finished in a single decisive battle
It was imposed by Greek conquerors
It was arranged by the Kushites from Nubia

items.explain: The transition to a unified state happened more gradually than ancient writers represented, and there is no contemporary record of Menes.

items.prompt: The Naqada culture's last predynastic phase saw something new that eventually became Egypt's full writing system. What was it?

options.label: Clay tablets copied from Mesopotamian scribes
Letters borrowed from the Phoenician alphabet
Knotted cords used to record harvests
Written symbols that were later developed

items.explain: The Naqada culture began using written symbols that eventually developed into a full system of hieroglyphs.

items.prompt: Imagine visiting Egypt in Predynastic times, when the climate was much less arid than today. What would large regions look like?

options.label: Sand dunes with almost no animals
Savanna crossed by herds of grazing animals
Dense rainforest along the coast
Frozen ground through the winter

items.explain: Large regions of Egypt were savanna traversed by herds of grazing ungulates.

items.prompt: Egypt reached its greatest power in the New Kingdom. What does the history say happened after that period?

options.label: It entered an era of slow decline
It started a second, higher peak
It collapsed completely in a single year
It split into three equal kingdoms

items.explain: After the New Kingdom, Egypt entered an era of slow decline.
